title: After 2 patient deaths and cell therapy durability concerns, Artiva cuts 94% of workforce
snippet: Artiva Biotherapeutics, which had been evaluating cell therapy AlloNK for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases, is exploring strategic options that could include dissolution and liquidation.

title: Teva closing New Jersey manufacturing facility, laying off 61 employees
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: EMSO 2026: Incyte a ‘firm contender’ in G12D pancreatic cancer race as early candidate shines
snippet: In a Phase 1 study, treatment with Incyte's KRAS G12D inhibitor in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy elicited an 89% confirmed objective response rate in patients with a type of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, leading analysts to draw comparisons with Revolution Medicines’ zoldonrasib.

title: Alphabet’s GV is one of biotech’s most influential corporate investors
snippet: The corporate investor arms of Eli Lilly, Sanofi and Pfizer have participated in billions worth of venture capital rounds, but GV is the industry’s biggest spender.

title: Novartis faces $1.9B hit from Avidity fail but maintains confidence in $12B buy
snippet: Novartis remains "very happy" with its $12 billion acquisition of Avidity Biosciences, despite a Phase 3 disappointment for the antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate del-desiran.

title: US biotechs take lion’s share of $54.5B VC money raised since 2025
snippet: Since 2025, U.S. biopharma companies have raised $37.2 billion—68% of total worldwide venture capital funding in the industry—with startups in the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston leading the way.

title: ESMO 2026: Merck’s Kelun-partnered ADC cuts death risk by over 30% in endometrial cancer
snippet: Sac-TMT significantly extended overall and progression-free survival for patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer by 6.9 months over chemotherapy in a Phase 3 trial—becoming the first TROP2-directed ADC to do so in this setting, Merck told BioSpace.

title: ESMO 2026: J&J delivers ‘immaculate’ early data for prostate cancer drug from Halda
snippet: JNJ-6143, which came from Johnson & Johnson’s $3 billion takeover of Halda Therapeutics in 2025, showed a 75% overall response rate in the Phase 1 readout.

title: Biotech IPOs raise $7.5B as sector’s performance rally flattens
snippet: While biopharma financing exit activity has remained strong through the third quarter, public-market performance for the same period was muted, with most of the yearly gains for the U.S. biotech-specific index largely driven by the first half of 2026.

title: ESMO 2026: Analysts warm to Merck, Moderna’s cancer vaccine after frustrating data leak
snippet: After sitting through the full presentation on the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial at the ESMO Congress over the weekend, analysts are more keen on the personalized mRNA cancer vaccine data that last week spurred a stock selloff for both partners.

title: ESMO 2026: Amgen’s Imdelltra slashes death risk by nearly 60% in small cell lung cancer
snippet: When used alongside AstraZeneca’s Imfinzi, the bispecific T cell engager Imdelltra extended survival by eight months versus Imfinzi alone in Phase 3 study testing the combo in a first-line maintenance setting—a potentially “practice-changing” outcome, according to Truist Securities.

title: Genmab’s ADC beats survival expectations in Phase 3 ovarian cancer trial
snippet: Extending both progression-free and overall survival, Genmab’s Rina-S “sets a high bar for future competition” in a market served by AbbVie, analysts said.

title: Neurogene, Taysha near finish line in ‘two-horse race’ for first Rett syndrome gene therapy
snippet: As both Taysha Gene Therapies and Neurogene warm up for an important year of readouts, the Rett syndrome community is hopeful of seeing a therapy that can truly change the disease's path.

title: Australia's clinical trial advantage gains ground amid U.S. uncertainty
snippet: CROs cite faster startup timelines, regulatory predictability and tax incentives as reasons for growing interest in Australia. State investments in manufacturing, translational research and advanced therapies aim to expand that advantage into a broader biotech ecosystem. The question remains whether Australia can supp...

title: BMS reveals death from septic pneumonia of multiple sclerosis patient in CAR T trial
snippet: The disclosure—which came ahead of a presentation of data from the Phase 1 Breakfree-2 study at the ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting—follows Bristol Myers Squibb’s late summer revelation that it had paused certain trials of zolacabtagene autoleucel.

title: Alnylam plans pivotal trial as Huntington’s drug notches ‘best-in-class knockdown’
snippet: RNAi specialist Alnylam Pharmaceuticals will advance the Huntington’s disease drug brezosiran into a placebo-controlled study in 2027 once regulatory alignment is achieved.

title: ESMO 2026: Tango trips on sinking response rates in pancreatic cancer but will move to Phase 3
snippet: A combination of Tango Therapeutics’ vopimetostat and Revolution Medicines’ recently approved Rasonque led to a response rate of 82% in an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial—a drop from 92% that was reported in June in fewer patients.

title: Roche flags ‘final opportunity’ for Germany to reestablish as a reliable investment location
snippet: Following the withdrawal of billions of dollars in investments from Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly, German lawmakers have proposed a clause to the country’s healthcare reforms set to take effect Jan. 1.

title: Gilead shops in IL-23, inking $1.3B upfront I&I deal with China’s PepStar
snippet: Gilead Sciences has picked up a new inflammatory disease program from China’s PepStar Therapeutics to pair with the Phase 2 inflammatory bowel disease asset emvistegrast.

title: ESMO 2026: Marengo's bispecific antibody shrinks 8 tumor types in Phase 2
snippet: Invikafusp alfa, a first-in-class dual T cell agonist, showed an objective response in various types of cancer, particularly among patients who did not respond to previous checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
